headline: High: unstructured can read/write files and egress allowlisted network, creating default data-leak and workflow-conflict risk with langchain4j as an upstream content source.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: langchain4j can surface model-generated or file-derived content, and unstructured reads documents from files; if langchain4j output is copied into documents or prompts, unstructured may ingest attacker-controlled text. No shared channel is documented, so this is inferred from the pair’s documented file/text surfaces rather than proven.
conditions: IF langchain4j outputs are pasted into documents that unstructured parses
IF an orchestrator feeds langchain4j text into unstructured without provenance checks
mitigations: Add a provenance header to every handoff file
Strip instructions from parsed text before downstream use
Review one sample document flow for prompt-like content
Disable automatic re-ingestion of generated files
requires-engineering: add content provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: unstructured has read_filesystem and allowlisted network egress, so it can transmit document contents off-box; langchain4j is a docs-only library with no egress, so the leakage path is one-sided but still plausible when both touch the same workspace. The pair lacks direct evidence of shared storage, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF both agents access the same document directory
IF unstructured sends parsed document text to its allowlisted endpoints
mitigations: Restrict unstructured to a scratch directory
Block network egress during parsing runs
Separate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces
Inspect one parsed sample for outbound fields
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: langchain4j is not runnable here, but unstructured can write_filesystem, spawn_subprocesses, and supports multiple instances. If an orchestrator uses langchain4j outputs to trigger unstructured jobs in the same directory, write conflicts and race conditions are plausible. Because langchain4j’s write surface is absent, this is an inferred overlap and uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF both agents target the same output directory
IF the orchestrator launches concurrent unstructured instances
mitigations: Assign separate output directories per agent
Run one unstructured job at a time
Check for existing lock files before writes
Rename outputs with unique run IDs
requires-engineering: add filesystem locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: langchain4j can generate text that unstructured may later parse or transform, and unstructured is a document-processing pipeline that can treat upstream text as authoritative input. There is no documented verification step between them, so a bad upstream output can cascade into incorrect downstream extraction or formatting. The interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF unstructured consumes langchain4j-produced documents or prompts
IF no human or automated verification step checks the intermediate output
mitigations: Add a validation step between agents
Compare extracted fields against source documents
Sample-check one downstream artifact per run
Reject malformed or instruction-like content
requires-engineering: implement schema validation on handoff

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent. langchain4j is an open-source library with no stated data handling, while unstructured exposes privacy-policy and docs endpoints and processes documents; absent a specific regulated data class, only a limited compliance gap is plausible.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is processed through unstructured
IF the deployment policy requires a specific residency or retention guarantee
mitigations: Review the privacy policy before deployment
Avoid regulated documents in the shared pipeline
Document retention settings for parsed outputs
Confirm where allowlisted endpoints are hosted
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing for regulated data
